chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'I deal with the merchants, so I prepare myself for the people, disliking that they see me in a state of destitution, so I purchase Al-Ghaliya.' He (peace be upon him) said, 'O Is'haq! A little of Al-Ghaliya suffices, and a lot of it is the same. Whoever takes a little of Al-Ghaliya constantly, that will suffice for him.' Is'haq said, 'And I buy from it during the year for ten dirhams, so I suffice myself with it, and its aroma remains fixed for a long duration.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on using expensive perfume for social status?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) validates the use of 'Al-Ghaliya' (a high-quality, often musk-based perfume) as a means of maintaining social dignity and avoiding the appearance of poverty, ruling that even a small, consistent amount suffices for this purpose. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on *Zuhur al-Husn* (manifesting beauty) and *Ihtiram al-Nafs* (self-respect) in public interactions, particularly for merchants, as a form of subtle worship and social responsibility. The hadith underscores that modest expenditure on personal grooming is not vanity but a legitimate practice to foster positive social perception and confidence.
